turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (CAREGIVER): Sorry doctor, the auto got stuck at the signal, that is why we are a bit late.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): No problem, come sit. Rohan, 29 years, correct?
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): Yes. Can we start, I am really tired and I have to get back.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): Sure. What is the main thing bothering you?
[SEG0005] person_3 (PATIENT): I am losing weight. And my heart races, like it will not slow down.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): Weight coming down, and a fast heartbeat. Since when, roughly?
[SEG0007] person_3 (PATIENT): Umm. About two months. I can't say the exact day it started, it just, uh, crept in.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): About two months then. How much weight have you lost?
[SEG0009] person_3 (PATIENT): I was 72 kilos. This morning the home scale said 64.
[SEG0010] person_1 (CAREGIVER): The nurse outside checked also, just before we came in. She wrote 63.8 on the slip. He already said 64, it is the same reading only.
[SEG0011] person_3 (PATIENT): Ya, whatever she wrote. Can we move on.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right. So we will take 63.8 kg as today's weight. Are you eating less to explain this?
[SEG0013] person_3 (PATIENT): No. I am eating more than usual only. More rice, more snacks, and still the weight comes down. It is irritating.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): Eating more and weight less. I will keep that in mind. Any sweating?
[SEG0015] person_3 (PATIENT): Lots. The shirt gets wet even in the AC. At work also.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): And the hands, do they shake?
[SEG0017] person_3 (PATIENT): They shake. The tea spills. Well, actually since a few weeks, not from the start.
[SEG0018] person_1 (CAREGIVER): Doctor, he also gets angry very fast these days. And he sleeps badly, I hear him walking around at 2 in the night.
[SEG0019] person_3 (PATIENT): I do not sleep badly. I sleep ok. I am just tired in the day. Stop adding things.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): Mm. I will not take the sleep as settled. The daytime tiredness you agree with. Any fever with all this?
[SEG0021] person_3 (PATIENT): No. No fever.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any chest pain?
[SEG0023] person_3 (PATIENT): No chest pain.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): Breathlessness?
[SEG0025] person_3 (PATIENT): Only if I climb stairs. Then I have to stop. Not otherwise.
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ok. What about the stomach, loose motions or vomiting?
[SEG0027] person_3 (PATIENT): No. Nothing like that.
[SEG0028] person_1 (CAREGIVER): One more thing. He cut his finger in the kitchen last week. It healed in five days, normal only.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any wound that is slow to heal, or was that the only cut?
[SEG0030] person_3 (PATIENT): That was it. Healed fine. Five days. Why are we even talking about a finger.
[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): Just checking. Some hormone problems make healing slow, this one did not. Any tablets you are taking?
[SEG0032] person_3 (PATIENT): Ya. The clinic doctor gave me propranalol. Forty mg, morning and night, for the fast heart.
[SEG0033] person_1 (CAREGIVER): He does not take the tablets on Sundays. I have seen the strip.
[SEG0034] person_3 (PATIENT): Not Sunday. It is Saturday. I skip Saturday because of the long BPO shift. Other days I take it.
[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): So propranolol 40 mg twice a day, by mouth, and the Saturday dose gets missed. Since when are you on it?
[SEG0036] person_3 (PATIENT): About three weeks. Uh, it helps a bit, the heart still races though.
[SEG0037] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me check you. Err, pulse is 118, regular. BP is 132 over 78.
[SEG0038] person_3 (PATIENT): The watch was showing hundred plus also. Fine.
[SEG0039] person_2 (DOCTOR): Palms are warm and sweaty. There is a fine shake in both hands. In the neck, the thyroid feels mildly enlarged, smooth.
[SEG0040] person_3 (PATIENT): Is that serious. Just tell me straight, I am too tired for hints.

[SEG0041] person_2 (DOCTOR): I am thinking aloud, so bear with me. Weight loss, eating more, racing heart, sweating, shaky hands, and a slightly big thyroid. This pattern fits an overactive thyroid. I cannot confirm it sitting here.
[SEG0042] person_1 (CAREGIVER): His sister has thyroid. She is on tablets for years.
[SEG0043] person_3 (PATIENT): Ya, Priya, my sister. Not me. I did not have any of this before.

[SEG0044] person_2 (DOCTOR): Family history matters here. Anxiety can cause a fast heart and sweating, but anxiety usually does not drop the weight while you eat more. So thyroid is my working impression, and anxiety stays on the side, not ruled out.
[SEG0045] person_3 (PATIENT): So what is the plan. I don't want a long lecture.
[SEG0046] person_2 (DOCTOR): We will do blood tests, TSH and the thyroid hormones, and an ECG today. Those I am booking now.
[SEG0047] person_3 (PATIENT): ECG for what. My heart is just fast, there is no pain.
[SEG0048] person_2 (DOCTOR): The ECG is to see the rhythm, because a fast heart can sometimes be an irregular one. It is a simple tracing, not a big test.
[SEG0049] person_2 (DOCTOR): If the blood tests do not settle the picture, we might do a thyroid scan later. Not booking it now. Only if it is still unclear.
[SEG0050] person_3 (PATIENT): And the tablet, I keep taking it or what.
[SEG0051] person_2 (DOCTOR): Continue the same propranolol, 40 mg twice daily. Try not to skip Saturday, the level dips and the heart runs faster. Cut down on tea and coffee, they push the pulse up.
[SEG0052] person_3 (PATIENT): Coffee is the only thing keeping me awake at the BPO. This is annoying.
[SEG0053] person_2 (DOCTOR): I know. Reduce it, not necessarily to zero. I will see you in two weeks with the reports. If you get chest pain or you faint, come earlier, do not wait.

spec.situation: Younger adult losing weight with a fast heartbeat, sweating, shaky hands, eats more than usual; hair thinning not mentioned; a sister has thyroid disease; blood tests and ECG planned.

traps.happens: A caregiver or relative reports observations ('the cut healed in five days', 'she sleeps badly', 'he does not take the tablets on Sundays'); the patient agrees, disagrees or corrects one point. The nurse also reports a measurement that the patient mentioned before.
traps.label_rule: reported_by follows who said it. A healing cut that healed normally is a negative finding (no slow-healing wounds) or nothing, NOT a symptom. A disputed fact is recorded with certainty disputed or as an uncertainty. A correction replaces the earlier value (Saturday, not Sunday).

features: hedged_plan: the doctor hedges ('we might do a scan if it does not settle', 'let's see in two weeks'). Conditional vs planned status must follow the words.
doctor_misses_topics: the doctor does not ask about everything; topics never discussed are simply absent (no invented denials, no allergy line if allergies were never mentioned).

omissions.text: Weight loss amount/details not recorded: from 72 kg previously to 63.8 kg today (about 8 kg loss).
Breathlessness detail missing: he has to stop when climbing stairs, but no breathlessness otherwise.

Negative finding missing: no diarrhea/loose motions or vomiting were reported together as 'nothing like that,' and no chest pain was reported; additionally, no fever was denied. Breathlessness is absent except on exertion.
Medication adherence detail recorded incompletely: the patient specifically misses the Saturday dose of propranolol (not Sunday), and has been taking it for about three weeks.
Response to medication missing: propranolol helps a bit, but the heart still races.
Family history detail missing: sister Priya has thyroid disease and has been on tablets for years.
